title: Colony-Sectoring Assay
author: Isaac Núñez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jsecnbe

steps.title: Grow overnight liquid cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate each bacterial strain (e.g., E.coli Top10 with CyOFP, mBeRFP, or sfGFP plasmids) into 5 mL LB broth containing the appropriate antibiotic (e.g., Kanamycin) and incubate at 37 °C with shaking overnight.

steps.title: Mix cultures proportionally
steps.instruction: Combine equal volumes of the overnight cultures; for example, mix 100 µL of the CyOFP culture, 100 µL of the mBeRFP culture, and 100 µL of the sfGFP culture.

steps.title: Dilute mixed culture
steps.instruction: Dilute the combined culture with fresh LB medium to obtain a lower cell density before plating.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 1:100 (one part culture to 99 parts LB).
Alternatively, dilute 1:10 000 (one part culture to 9 999 parts LB).

steps.title: Spot inoculum onto agar
steps.instruction: Place a small volume of the diluted mixture onto an LB agar plate containing the same antibiotic(s) used for the cultures.

substeps.instruction: Deposit a 0.5 µL drop of the diluted mixture in the center of the plate.
Alternatively, deposit a 0.3 µL drop of the diluted mixture in the center of the plate.

steps.title: Incubate plates for colony growth
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated plates at room temperature for 2 – 10 days, or at 37 °C for a shorter period, noting that temperature strongly influences colony growth rate.
